chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ali ibn Hadid from Murram narrated, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Fasting in Al-Madinah and standing (in prayer) near the pillars is not obligatory, but whoever wishes may fast, for it is better for him. The only obligatory things are the five daily prayers and fasting the month of Ramadan. So increase your prayers in this mosque as much as you can, for it is better for you. And know that a man may be shrewd in worldly affairs, so it is said, 'How shrewd so-and-so is!' So how about the one who is shrewd in the affairs of his Hereafter?'
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between obligatory and recommended fasting in Medina according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between the obligatory pillars of Islam—specifically the five daily prayers and fasting in Ramadan—and the recommended (mustahabb) acts of fasting in Medina or standing in prayer near the pillars. He encourages believers to maximize voluntary prayers in the Sacred Mosque, using the metaphor of worldly wisdom to highlight the superior 'cleverness' of one who secures their Hereafter through such devotion.
